historical_references.reference: Jadus, son of Balthasar, was a Babylonian priest who converted to Christianity and became a bishop in the early Church. He is said to have lived during the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD) and was martyred during the Great Persecution.
historical_references.context: Babylonian priest who converted to Christianity and became a bishop during the time of Emperor Diocletian's persecution.

historical_references.reference: Saint Jadus was a bishop of Bordeaux in France during the 6th century AD. He is venerated as a patron saint of the diocese and is said to have been a missionary to the Frisians, a Germanic people along the North Sea coast.
historical_references.context: Bishop of Bordeaux who was a missionary to the Frisians during this time period.
